Question_text: RSL manufactures paint using flow production. Last year it produced 10 million litres of paint. RSL has 6 managers and 80 employees working in its factory. The managers use different leadership styles. RSL uses email and telephone calls as its methods of internal communication. The Operations Manager wants to understand why some manufacturing businesses are relocating their operations to other countries.
Sub_topic: Features, benefits, limitations: job, batch, flow production
Features of leadership: autocratic, democratic, laissez-faire
Benefits, limitations of methods, including IT

Parts.part_text: Identify two benefits to a business of using flow production.
Identify two reasons why people work.
Outline one advantage of RSL using each of the following methods of internal communication. Email: Telephone calls:
Explain two leadership styles RSL's managers might use.
Explain two factors a manufacturing business should consider when relocating its operations to another country. Which factor is likely to be the most important? Justify your answer.

Question_text: Mitchell is an entrepreneur. He wants to start up a business selling books. As part of his business plan Mitchell has carried out some market research. An extract is shown in Fig. 2.1. Mitchell will use microfinance as a source of finance. He wants to know whether the opportunities of using ecommerce for a new business are greater than the threats.
image: Fig. 2.1 displays an extract from Mitchell's market research data for 2023. It consists of two charts. Chart 1 is a pie chart titled 'Type of people reading books', showing percentages for 'Older people' (27%), 'Adults' (20%), 'Children' (35%), and 'Students' (18%). Chart 2 is a bar chart titled 'Book sales by type (million)', with a y-axis ranging from 0 to 60 million and categories on the x-axis: 'Electronic books' (approx 20 million), 'Audio books' (approx 10 million), 'Paperbacks' (approx 55 million), and 'Hardbacks' (approx 15 million).
Sub_topic: Contents of business plan, assistance to entrepreneurs

Parts.part_text: Define 'entrepreneur'.
Define 'business plan'.
Outline one advantage and one disadvantage to Mitchell of using microfinance as a source of finance.
Explain how the market research data in Chart 1 and Chart 2 in Fig. 2.1 could help Mitchell when making decisions.
Do you think the opportunities of ecommerce for a new business are greater than the threats? Justify your answer.

Question_text: JTA is a public limited company. It sells holidays in a mass market. The business has 44 shops and 200 employees. The Finance Director is considering ways a business can increase its profit. She has been asked to analyse JTA's financial performance using ratio analysis. An extract from JTA's financial statements is shown in Table 3.1.
image: Table 3.1, titled 'Extract from JTA's financial statements for 2023 ($ million)', shows financial data. It has three rows: 'Revenue' (900), 'Profit' (100), and 'Capital employed' (800).
Sub_topic: Features: sole traders, partnerships, private/public limited companies, franchises, joint ventures
Ratios: gross profit margin, profit margin, return on capital employed, current ratio, acid test ratio
Different objectives: survival, growth, profit, market share

Parts.part_text: Define 'capital employed'.
Calculate JTA's return on capital employed (ROCE). Show your working.
Outline two benefits to JTA of selling in a mass market.
Explain one advantage and one disadvantage of JTA being a public limited company.
Do you think increasing prices is the best way for a business to increase its profit? Justify your answer.

Question_text: FSW is a multinational company with operations in 6 countries. It manufactures steel for use in the construction industry. Quality assurance is used to ensure quality production. FSW has many stakeholder groups who are interested in its activities. The Managing Director knows FSW's business creates external costs. She is aware that pressure groups try to influence business decisions.
Unit: UNIT 6: External influences on business activity

Parts.part_text: Define 'external costs'.
Identify one objective each of the following stakeholder groups might have: Employees: Customers:
Identify four ways a pressure group might try to influence business decisions.
Explain one possible benefit and one possible drawback to a country of having FSW (a multinational company) operating there.
Do you think quality assurance is the best way for a business to achieve quality production? Justify your answer.
